failedHostedAcceptanceIdentity.failure: accountDeletion.spec.ts:35 — deletion must complete; stopped at {"error":"deletion_failed"}, expected 200 received 500

rootCause.classification: Preview database lineage parity gap — NOT an application defect
rootCause.detail: The deployed code calls yorisou_account_deletion_erase_database(uuid, text, text, integer), created by 202608010110/111. Those are PRODUCTION_LINEAGE and were never applied to Preview, which only received the PREVIEW lineage. The RPC could not resolve.

previewBeforeState.erase_database: ONLY yorisou_account_deletion_erase_database(p_owner_account_id text) — the weak, owner-only signature

localReproduction.environment: disposable PostgreSQL 17 with Supabase platform roles and default privileges, built from repository SQL (baseline + PREVIEW lineage)
localReproduction.baselineBodyFidelity: the reconstructed weak erase_database body md5 is 4ece4f3e670ef13b673d73fba0a9876c — BYTE-IDENTICAL to live Preview, so the guarded rename was validated against the real baseline
localReproduction.baselineFailureShape: ERROR: function public.yorisou_account_deletion_erase_database(uuid, unknown, unknown, integer) does not exist — the same missing-RPC shape that produced the hosted 500

appendOnlyFamilyClassification.path: B — the families are PRESENT in Preview
absent: yorisou_candidate_events — carries no user identity; NOT_APPLICABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_ERASURE; not referenced by this migration
appendOnlyFamilyClassification.blockingTriggers: no_mutate/no_truncate on daily_state_record_versions, daily_state_history_events, values_assessment_versions, values_assessment_events, via yorisou_dci_block_mutation and yorisou_values_block_mutation
appendOnlyFamilyClassification.consequence: without the governed exception those triggers refuse the erasure — the M4 defect 202608010109 was written to resolve. The applicable 109 behaviour is therefore ported here under existence checks.

migrationDesign.productionMigrationsApplied: NONE — 109/110/111 were neither executed nor registered in Preview, and their files were not copied
migrationDesign.preservedPreviewBody: the live owner-only function is RENAMED to yorisou_account_deletion_erase_database_unchecked(text), not rewritten: its subset-aware plan is what makes erasure correct in an environment lacking some Production families. The rename is guarded by an md5 precondition and fails closed if the live body is not the reviewed baseline.
establishes: yorisou_account_deletion_executor_claim brought to the final post-P111 body so the claim returns job_id
migrationDesign.governedException: yorisou_dci_block_mutation and yorisou_values_block_mutation now return OLD for a DELETE only when yorisou_account_erasure_authorized(<the row's owner>) is true, re-derived from durable state; every other mutation is refused exactly as before. No general trigger bypass.
migrationDesign.idempotent: applied twice locally and twice against live Preview; second application is a no-op
migrationDesign.selfAsserting: the migration raises if the strong signature is absent, either weak signature survives, the unchecked implementation is missing, service_role cannot execute the wrapper, service_role CAN execute the unchecked implementation, or any erasure function is reachable by PUBLIC/anon/authenticated

runtimeReadiness.fact: por1SchemaReadiness.ACCOUNT_ERASURE_AUTHORITY, always present as a boolean in /api/build-identity
runtimeReadiness.whyItWasMissing: the four existing readiness flags all read true during the failed acceptance; none covered the erasure family, so the application called an RPC its database could not satisfy and reported a generic 500 mid-deletion
runtimeReadiness.failClosed: claimDeletionExecutor refuses BEFORE claiming a new job when the flag is not exactly 'on', returning account_erasure_authority_schema_unready. There is deliberately no fallback to the weak owner-only RPC — that would trade an honest refusal for an authority bypass.
runtimeReadiness.alreadyIrreversibleJobs: keep governed resume semantics; refusing there would abandon a partially executed deletion
runtimeReadiness.unitTests: 9/9 — including the enumeration proving no fallback mode is expressible

consequenceRecordedNotFixed.finding: after the parity migration, `compile-promotion.mjs --check` REFUSES to compile from a post-parity Preview catalogue
reasons: yorisou_dci_block_mutation() and yorisou_values_block_mutation() now differ in body from Production, and the compiler refuses to promote a function that exists in Production with a different body

yorisou_account_erasure_authorized, yorisou_account_erasure_job_valid and yorisou_ct_eq are not placed in any promotion group, because they are created by the hand-written 109/110/111 rather than by the generated set
consequenceRecordedNotFixed.assessment: this is the compiler behaving correctly. It is reporting a true fact: Preview is no longer a clean generation source for the 101-108 promotion set. The already-generated and checked-in promotion migrations are unaffected, and the drift gate against the ORIGINAL pre-parity Preview catalogue still reports 0.
consequenceRecordedNotFixed.disposition: RECORDED for the Founder. Regenerating the promotion set from Preview now requires a decision about how the compiler should model the overlay families; not attempted here.
